questions.stem: A surveyor measures the angle of elevation to the top of a tower from point $A$ as $35°$ and from point $B$ (which is $50\text{ m}$ closer to the tower) as $50°$. To find the height of the tower, you should:

options.text: Set up two equations using $\tan$ and solve simultaneously
Use the sine rule directly on triangle $ABT$
Average the two angles and use a single $\tan$ equation

questions.explanation: Let the height be $h$ and the distance from $B$ to the base be $d$. Then $\tan 50° = \frac{h}{d}$ and $\tan 35° = \frac{h}{d + 50}$. Solving these simultaneously gives $h$.
